content.title: Garrison Street Mural
content.summary: The Garrison Street Mural, titled \"Nature Notes: Ralston Creek,\" is a community-driven project aimed at enhancing public art and fostering connections among residents in Arvada. Created by local artist Catie Michel, the 1,527-square-foot mural features native flora and fauna of the Ralston Creek area and includes Augmented Reality elements for an interactive learning experience. The project involved community engagement through workshops and painting days, reflecting the neighborhood's vision and promoting a sense of identity and pride.
content.body:
![colorful mural along and trail underpass next to a creek](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=5692)

## Project Overview

The Garrison Street Mural is a dynamic, community-led project designed to enhance our city's art footprint and foster community connection through the power of public art. Funded by the [Arvada Arts and Culture Commission](/488), this project aims to bring life and creativity to the Garrison Street underpass. The mural is located at approximately [5890 Garrison St.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/LPek49SgXQTYHvbp6) along the scenic Ralston Creek Trail, just south of the Carr Street and Brooks Drive intersection and west of Ralston Central Park.

The 1,527-square-foot mural, titled "Nature Notes: Ralston Creek," celebrates the natural beauty and rich history of the Ralston Creek area while also educating viewers about ecosystem health and conservation.

## Artist Selection

![Garrison Street Mural artist Catie Michel](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=5004)After a thorough selection process, [local artist Catie Michel](https://www.catiemichel.com/) was awarded the commission. Catie, a resident Coloradan muralist and science illustrator, proposed a design that incorporates local flora and fauna observed by trail visitors. Her mural serves as both a field guide to the area's ecological richness and a celebration of the interconnectedness of all communities— human and more-than-human.

## Interactive Elements

The mural features a dynamic above-and-underwater view of a freshwater Front Range ecosystem, showcasing species native to the Ralston Creek area. To further enhance the educational aspect, the mural incorporates Augmented Reality (AR) elements. Viewers can use their phones to scan a QR code and learn more about the species depicted in the mural, blending art with technology to create an interactive learning experience.

## Community Engagement

This project is not just about beautifying a wall — it's about building community. The Flower Street Folks Neighborhood Group, who first proposed this project as part of the [City of Arvada's Neighborhood Grant Program](/485), envisioned the mural as a means to increase neighborhood connection and reduce loneliness. When it became clear the scope of the project was too large for the neighborhood grant program, the Arts and Culture Commission stepped in to fund the mural.

Michel honored the neighborhood's vision by inviting the community to actively participate in the mural's creation. Residents had the chance to join in the painting process during community painting days and nature workshops to foster a stronger sense of neighborhood identity and pride.

## Educational Workshops and Community Paint Days

In addition to the mural itself, Michel conducted a series of field science workshops along the Ralston Creek Trail. These workshops helped guide participants in observing and documenting local wildlife, plants, and insects, and the insights gathered will shape the final mural design. This collaborative effort ensures that the mural reflects the community's perspective and knowledge, deepening the connection between participants and their natural environment.

Nature workshops were held Sept. 1, 7 and 8, 2024. Workshops were free and open to the public. Catie also hosting two community paint days on Sept. 27 and 29.
